jobs.description:
Description

At Amazon Selection and Catalog Systems (ASCS), our mission is to power the online buying experience for customers worldwide so they can find, discover, and buy any product they want. We innovate on behalf of our customers to ensure uniqueness and consistency of product identity and to infer relationships between products in Amazon Catalog to drive the selection gateway for the search and browse experiences on the website. We're solving a fundamental AI challenge: establishing product identity and relationships at unprecedented scale. Using Generative AI, Visual Language Models (VLMs), and multimodal reasoning, we determine what makes each product unique and how products relate to one another across Amazon's catalog. The scale is staggering: billions of products, petabytes of multimodal data, millions of sellers, dozens of languages, and infinite product diversity—from electronics to groceries to digital content.

The research challenges are immense. GenAI and VLMs hold transformative promise for catalog understanding, but we operate where traditional methods fail: ambiguous problem spaces, incomplete and noisy data, inherent uncertainty, reasoning across both images and textual data, and explaining decisions at scale. Establishing product identities and groupings requires sophisticated models that reason across text, images, and structured data—while maintaining accuracy and trust for high-stakes business decisions affecting millions of customers daily.

Amazon's Item and Relationship Platform group is looking for an innovative and customer-focused applied scientist to help us make the world's best product catalog even better. In this role, you will partner with technology and business leaders to build new state-of-the-art algorithms, models, and services to infer product-to-product relationships that matter to our customers. You will pioneer advanced GenAI solutions that power next-generation agentic shopping experiences, working in a collaborative environment where you can experiment with massive data from the world's largest product catalog, tackle problems at the frontier of AI research, rapidly implement and deploy your algorithmic ideas at scale, across millions of customers.

Key job responsibilities

Key Job Responsibilities Include

Formulate open research problems at the intersection of GenAI, multimodal reasoning, and large-scale information retrieval—defining the scientific questions that transform ambiguous, real-world catalog challenges into publishable, high-impact research
Push the boundaries of VLMs, foundation models, and agentic architectures by designing novel approaches to product identity, relationship inference, and catalog understanding—where the problem complexity (billions of products, multimodal signals, inherent ambiguity) demands methods that don't yet exist
Advance the science of efficient model deployment—developing distillation, compression, and LLM/VLM serving optimization strategies that preserve frontier-level multimodal reasoning in compact, production-grade architectures while dramatically reducing latency, cost, and infrastructure footprint at billion-product scale
Make frontier models reliable—advancing uncertainty calibration, confidence estimation, and interpretability methods so that frontier-scale GenAI systems can be trusted for autonomous catalog decisions impacting millions of customers daily
Own the full research lifecycle from problem formulation through production deployment—designing rigorous experiments over petabytes of multimodal data, iterating on ideas rapidly, and seeing your research directly improve the shopping experience for hundreds of millions of customers
Shape the team's research vision by defining technical roadmaps that balance foundational scientific inquiry with measurable product impact
Mentor scientists and engineers on advanced ML techniques, experimental design, and scientific rigor—building deep organizational capability in GenAI and multimodal AI
Represent the team in the broader science community—publishing findings, delivering tech talks, and staying at the forefront of GenAI, VLM, and agentic system research

Basic Qualifications

PhD, or Master's degree and 4+ years of CS, CE, ML or related field experience
Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language
2+ years of building machine learning models or developing algorithms for business application experience

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with LLMs, VLMs, foundation models, or large-scale deep learning systems—including multimodal pretraining, fine-tuning, RLHF, prompt engineering, or agentic architectures
Experience with LLM/VLM serving optimization, including model distillation, quantization, pruning, speculative decoding, or other model compression and efficient inference techniques
Experience with explainable AI, model interpretability, or uncertainty quantification
Strong experimental design skills and statistical analysis expertise
Track record of deploying ML models at scale in production environments processing billions of data points
Publications in top-tier venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR, ICCV, EMNLP, ACL, NAACL, COLING, KDD, SIGMOD, WWW, AAAI, or similar
Excellent written, verbal communication & data presentation skills

jobs.description:
Company Description

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

The Forward Deployed Engineer, Voice AI Agent Engineering designs, builds, ships, and operates voice AI agents whose core behavior is model-driven rather than explicitly authored — conversational and agentic experiences that interpret caller intent over a live audio channel, reason over context, invoke tools, and act on the caller's behalf. The engineer works across the full lifecycle: shaping ambiguous call flows and telephony requirements into precise specifications, authoring the instructions and prompts that govern voice agent behavior, proving through automated evaluation that the result behaves correctly on real calls. This is not a machine learning or AI research role — the engineer does not train foundation or speech models — but it is distinct from traditional software engineering, where systems follow deterministic call-flow logic rather than selecting execution paths at runtime.

Two things follow, and voice makes both harder. First, the agent's most important logic often lives in natural language — instructions, prompts, tool descriptions, and guardrails — which must be engineered, versioned, and reviewed with the same discipline as code, while also holding up under what a spoken channel adds: turn-taking, barge-in, and disambiguating what speech recognition got wrong. Second, because behavior is probabilistic and happens live on a call, correctness is established by measuring behavior at scale — including latency, containment, and transcription accuracy — rather than by asserting fixed outputs, making automated evaluation a first-class engineering activity rather than a quality-assurance afterthought. The engineer owns the correctness of what ships to a live caller, whether a human or an agent produced it.

What You Get To Do In This Role

Build voice AI agents. Design and ship agentic voice applications — intent interpretation, multi-step reasoning, tool invocation, and action on the caller's behalf — together with the CTI, CCaaS, and telephony integrations that make them usable in production.
Design AI-driven autonomous voice workflows. Decompose call flows and business processes into the steps and decision points a voice agent can execute — determining where autonomy is appropriate, where a live-agent handoff is required, and how misrecognition, retries, and escalation are handled.
Engineer for what voice demands. Build experiences that hold context across turns, manage barge-in and interruption, recover gracefully from speech-recognition error, disambiguate caller intent, and confirm before consequential actions — all within the latency budget a live call imposes.
Author and maintain voice agent instructions. Write, structure, and version the system instructions, role definitions, tool descriptions, guardrails, and escalation rules that govern voice agent behavior — as engineering artifacts under review and regression coverage, not configuration text.
Engineer prompts for reliability rather than demo quality. Iterate prompts against measured call outcomes: task decomposition, golden call transcripts, structured output schemas, grounding and citation, graceful hand-back to a human agent, and the token and latency cost that directly shapes caller experience.
Build automated evaluation and test non-deterministic voice behavior. Design and operate the evaluation that makes change safe on a live channel — golden call datasets, multi-turn conversation suites, model-as-judge scoring calibrated to human QA review, CI gates, and drift detection — plus adversarial, jailbreak, grounding, and tool-selection testing specific to voice.
Specify precisely and direct AI coding agents. Convert customer call-flow and telephony requirements into testable specifications with explicit scope, constraints, and acceptance criteria; decompose work into agent-sized tasks; and review agent output for correctness and maintainability. You own the result regardless of what produced it.
Deliver as a forward deployed engineer, embedded in the voice stack. Work directly inside a customer's telephony, CTI, and CCaaS environment — building against their call data, integrations, and channels, tuning instructions and evaluation sets against live traffic, and returning with evidence that improves the product.
Own quality, safety, and reliability on live calls. Monitor call containment, hallucination, unsafe actions, and transcription accuracy; defend against prompt injection and data leakage on live calls; and feed production call failures back into specifications and evaluation sets.
Collaborate across product, design, and engineering. Partner with product managers, designers and platform teams to define success criteria, align on tradeoffs, and communicate capability and risk clearly

Qualifications

To Be Successful in This Role:

A demonstrated track record of building, shipping, and operating production voice applications, including hands-on delivery of AI-native voice agent features that real callers depend on rather than demos. Direct experience authoring agentic instructions and prompts for voice, designing AI-driven autonomous call workflows, and building the evaluation and testing that verifies them against live call traffic, is required. Willingness to work directly with customers in a forward deployed capacity, embedded in their voice and contact center environment, is required. At least 10 years of experience in software engineering with at least 2 years of experience in deploying contemporary AI solutions at customers.

Education:Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. Advanced degrees or certifications are a plus but are not a substitute for a demonstrated record of shipping reliable, production voice AI agents.

Key Competencies, Skills, And Experience

Software engineering fundamentals. Strong command of data structures, algorithms, system design, APIs, data modeling, and testing.
AI native voice application development. Hands-on experience building applications where model-driven behavior is central — agent orchestration at the application layer, tool and function calling, context assembly, grounding against enterprise data, and handling the latency, cost, and failure modes unique to a live audio channel.
AI-driven autonomous workflow design. Demonstrated experience designing workflows in which voice agents carry out multi-step call processes with limited supervision: call-flow decomposition, decision points and autonomy boundaries, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, exception and retry handling, and observability over what the agent did and why.
Voice and telephony platform expertise. Practical experience with telephony integration, speech recognition and synthesis, and streaming audio — including the barge-in, turn-taking, and confirmation patterns a live call requires.
Agentic instruction authoring. Demonstrated skill writing and maintaining the natural-language logic that governs voice agent behavior — instructions, role definitions, tool descriptions, guardrails, and refusal and escalation rules — with versioning, review, and regression coverage applied as they would be to code.
Prompt engineering. Intent-driven prompt design tuned for voice: decomposition, golden and few-shot examples, structured output and schema enforcement, grounding and citation, and disciplined iteration against call-level evaluation results rather than impressions.
Evaluation and testing of non-deterministic voice systems. Ability to build measurable frameworks assessing call quality, agent behavior, tool-selection accuracy, and regression risk — golden call datasets, scenario suites, model-as-judge scoring with human QA calibration, continuous evaluation pipelines, and drift detection — plus adversarial, jailbreak, and grounding testing.
Specification precision and architectural judgment. Ability to define call-flow problems rigorously enough that another engineer or an AI agent implements them correctly, and to decide soundly when to solve a problem in code, in instructions, or by delegating to an agent.
Safety, security, and data handling. Working knowledge of risks specific to AI-integrated voice applications — prompt injection, sensitive-data and call-recording leakage, over-broad tool access, unsafe autonomous action — translated into concrete guardrails, least-privilege controls, and monitoring.
Forward deployed delivery and stakeholder communication. Comfort working directly with customers inside their telephony environment under incomplete information and fixed timelines, judgment about when a fast local solution is right and when to hold out for the durable one, and credibility communicating capability, limitation, and risk to non-engineers.

Desired Experience

Forward deployed or customer-embedded delivery. Prior work as a forward deployed engineer, solution engineer, or in professional services, delivering software inside a customer's environment.
Voice and contact center technology. Telephony and contact center platforms, IVR, speech recognition and synthesis, streaming audio, and real-time latency optimization.
Conversation design partnership. Experience working alongside conversation or content designers, contributing to dialogue flow, tone, and error-recovery design.
Evaluation and observability tooling. Evaluation frameworks, prompt and instruction management tooling, tracing for LLM applications, and analysis of production call transcripts at scale.
Enterprise domain depth. Customer service, contact center operations, sales, or enterprise workflow, at a depth sufficient to challenge a requirement rather than only implement it.
Years of Experience. At least 10 years of experience in software engineering with at least 2 years of experience in deploying contemporary AI solutions at customers

jobs.description:
Location: Kirkland, WA (HQ) — remote-first, hybrid · Type: Full-time

Compensation: $180,000–$240,000 base salary · 10–20% target bonus · founding equity grant, 4-year vest

About Hussh

Hussh's mission: make information — especially private personal information — a real financial asset for the human it belongs to, with the human in control. The technology company builds private personal AI (Private Agent One, iMoney, the puppy home supercomputer); the asset manager runs permanent capital on the world's fastest growers of absolute free cash flow.

Our privacy-law campaign runs on evidence. The data behind it — the campaign experimentation scoreboard, the policy data programs, the analysis that goes in front of lawmakers and regulators — is built by Anoushka Gehani, our Founding Public Policy Data Scientist: a founding talent carrying a senior-sized mandate, early in a journey we intend to be long. She doesn't need a manager. She needs senior craft around her. That's this role. Hussh is 100% privately owned and profitable — founder-funded, no outside investors — and we hire the best and pay the best. The seat sits inside the biggest bet we know how to make: AI, personal superintelligence for everybody, on the best supercomputers we can build — and every number you defend has to create real value for the human it describes, because that value, delivered honestly, is what becomes equity for everyone who works with us, invests with us, or does business with us.

The role

Mission: the senior craft layer of the data function — build the evidence engine, and make the people around you stronger.

You are hired as a multiplier, not a manager: one of the first 1–2 senior data scientists / data engineers forming the senior layer of our data function. Your primary customer is the evidence engine behind the policy fight; your reach is the whole company — product analytics, growth data, fund data hygiene — served on a real service basis, not favors.

What you'll do

- Build and harden the data engineering backbone: pipelines, experiment tracking, campaign data infrastructure — documented, tested, reproducible. Built to last, not to demo.
- Red-pen every analysis that leaves the company. Nothing reaches a lawmaker, a regulator, or an allocator that a senior hasn't reviewed. No exceptions, no drama.
- Mentor as a first-class output: pair reviews, methodology coaching, pipelines written so well a junior can own them in six months — then hand them over. Your metric is a founding data scientist demonstrably stronger every quarter.
- Guard the firewall in both directions: when the data doesn't support the position, you say so — loudly. The evidence program's credibility is the asset; you are its custodian.
- Serve the company's wider data needs on agreed service levels: the product team's analytics, the growth team's experiments, the funds' data hygiene.

What success looks like in 6 months

- The campaign and policy data pipelines run to a standard a senior would defend in public — and Anoushka's analyses are visibly sharper for your partnership.
- One data review gate exists and holds: every external analysis passes a senior's red pen.
- The evidence engine runs on a cadence the policy team can plan against: data in, verified analysis out.
- The company's data needs have one address — yours — with service levels instead of favors.

What you bring — musts

- Senior-level data science or data engineering with real scale behind you: pipelines serving millions, experiments at statistical seriousness, or ML systems in production.
- You have mentored a junior into a mid-level or senior — and can tell us the story. Mentorship is the job, not a nice-to-have.
- Statistical honesty under pressure. Advocacy environments test this; you have passed the test before.
- You build for handoff: documentation, tests, reproducibility — the opposite of a hero dependency.

Nice to have

- Experimentation-platform or campaign-analytics experience.
- Policy, civic-tech, or research-institution data work — evidence built for skeptical external readers.
- The founding dynamic instinct: you respect domain context and campaign instincts in a younger founder, and your seniority in craft never becomes seniority in the room.

What we offer

$180,000–$240,000 base, a 10–20% target bonus, and a founding equity grant on a 4-year vest. A small, senior team by design — leverage, not headcount — where your craft compounds into a founder's growth and a campaign's credibility, at a company whose entire thesis is that information belongs to the human it describes.

How to apply

Apply here on LinkedIn with your resume and a short note answering one question: describe a time the data told you something your side didn't want to hear — and what you did.

jobs.description:
About Persona

Persona is the configurable identity platform built for businesses in a digital-first world. Verifying individuals and organizations is harder — but more important — than ever, with AI enabling fraudsters to launch sophisticated accounts at scale and regulations evolving rapidly.

We’ve built Persona to support practically every use case and industry — that’s why we’re able to serve a wide range of leading companies. For example, Reddit relies on Persona for age assurance and verification to comply with online safety regulations, protecting younger users while maintaining a seamless experience. Meanwhile, OpenAI relies on Persona to keep bad actors out, protecting one of the world’s most powerful AI platforms from large-scale abuse in a time when AI is reshaping the way we work and live.

We’re growing rapidly and looking for exceptional people to join us!

About The Role

Proving who someone is online has never been harder or more important. You'll research how to detect fraud and verify identities more accurately. Your work will include detecting AI-generated and manipulated images, understanding how models perform across populations, and finding patterns in how attackers behave.

You bring depth in at least one of computer vision, mathematics and statistics, or identity verification and fraud prevention. You test ideas with focused experiments and follow what the results show. You'll work with our ML and engineering teams to turn your findings into defenses for real customers, and you'll get to publish your work.

What You’ll Do At Persona

Lead research on open problems in identity verification and fraud prevention, using focused experiments to test new ideas quickly.
Develop methods to detect manipulated documents, AI-generated images and emerging fraud attacks.
Evaluate how reliably our models perform across different populations
Uncover the patterns in verification data that reveal fraud, and prove they're real signal and not noise.
Calibrate model confidence and measure fraud events with limited labeled data.
Partner with ML and engineering to turn research prototypes into production models.
Publish at top venues such as CVPR, NeurIPS and USENIX Security, and stay active in the research community.

What You’ll Bring To Persona

Deep expertise in one of the following:
Computer vision: research in image forensics, face analysis, generative models or representation learning.
Mathematics and statistics: strong foundation in areas such as probability, statistical inference, optimization, or applied mathematics, with experience applying it to empirical research.
Identity or fraud prevention: Experience researching identity verification, biometrics, fraud detection, out-of-distribution detection, adversarial behavior, or closely related security problems.

A PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Mathematics, Statistics, or a related technical field is strongly preferred. We will also consider candidates with an MS and an exceptional research record.
A demonstrated record of peer-reviewed publications in relevant conferences or journals, with substantive contributions to the research.
Independently lead research, design rigorous experiments, and use results including negative or unexpected findings to guide next steps.
Clear communication, including the ability to explain experimental design, findings, and limitations to technical and non-technical audiences.

Nice to haves

Research on deepfakes, presentation attacks or adversarial robustness.
Experience with noisy, imbalanced real-world data.
Experience shipping ML research to production.

Benefits And Perks

For full-time US-based employees (excluding internship and contractor opportunities), Persona offers a wide range of benefits, including medical, dental, and vision, 3% 401(k) contribution, unlimited PTO, quarterly mental health days, family planning benefits, professional development stipend, wellness benefits, among others.

For full-time UK employees, Persona offers a wide range of benefits, including private medical insurance, dental insurance, a 6% employer pension contribution, unlimited PTO, a monthly wellness stipend, professional development stipend, co-working stipend, and more.

As part of our interview process, all candidates will be asked to verify their identity with Persona. This step is used solely to confirm that candidates are who they say they are, and will have no impact on hiring decisions.

jobs.description:
🚀 Join the Future of Commerce with Whatnot!

Whatnot is the largest live shopping platform in North America and Europe to buy, sell, and discover the things you love. Whether it's trading cards, fashion, electronics, or live plants, our sellers are building real businesses across hundreds of categories. We're building live commerce at a scale that's never been done in the West, and there's no playbook to copy. The people here are shaping how an entirely new industry develops.

As a remote co-located team, we're inspired by our values and anchored in hubs across the US, UK, Ireland, Poland, Germany, and Australia. We move fast, stay close to our users, and focus on the work that drives the most impact.

We're one of the fastest growing marketplaces and were recently named the #1 Best Startup Employer in America by Forbes. Check out the latest Whatnot updates on our news and engineering blogs and join us as we enable anyone to turn their passion into a business and bring people together through commerce.

💻 Role

The Seller Merchant team helps sellers bring inventory onto Whatnot, organize it effectively, and make it easier to sell. That includes products, listings, variants, catalog, taxonomy, inventory creation, seller workflows, and integrations such as Shopify.

Our sellers range from someone going live for the first time on their phone to sophisticated merchants managing large inventories across multiple systems. They also operate across very different categories, countries, and selling formats. The right product experience for one seller may be completely wrong for another.

As a Data Scientist on Seller Merchant, you'll use data to help us understand those differences and build better products for sellers. Your work will ultimately help sellers become more productive, grow their businesses, and bring more high-quality supply to the marketplace.

You'll

Identify and prioritize the highest-impact opportunities to improve seller success. Use product analysis, opportunity sizing, and strategic thinking to understand where changes to seller workflows can have the largest impact on activation, inventory creation, selling efficiency, and GMV.
Design and evaluate experiments across the seller experience. Partner with Product, Engineering, and Design to turn ambiguous questions into testable hypotheses, define success metrics and guardrails, design rigorous experiments, and translate results into product decisions.
Develop the analytical frameworks that shape product strategy. Go beyond answering incoming questions by proactively identifying opportunities, defining new ways to measure seller success, and helping the team decide what to build next.
Understand how different sellers need different products. Analyze differences across seller size, maturity, category, country, inventory type, and selling format, and help determine when a single experience works versus when we should build for distinct seller segments.
Help us make good decisions even when the data isn't perfect. Supply-side problems often involve smaller samples, heterogeneous populations, or decisions where data provides important evidence without giving a black-and-white answer. You'll apply analytics, causal inference, and other statistical approaches where appropriate, while partnering closely with product leaders to combine evidence with sound judgment.

You'll be deeply embedded with the product team, but you'll also have meaningful independence to develop your own hypotheses, challenge existing thinking, and use data to influence where the team invests.

We offer flexibility to work from home or from one of our global office hubs, and we value in-person time for planning, problem-solving, and connection. Team members in this role must live within commuting distance of our New York, San Francisco hub.

👋 You

People who do well at Whatnot tend to be comfortable figuring things out as they go, biased toward action, and genuinely curious about what they're building. They care more about outcomes than credit and stay close to the product and the people using it.

As Our Next Data Scientist, You Should Have 5+ Years Of Experience In Product Data Science, Analytics, Or a Closely Related Field, Plus

A Bachelor's degree in Statistics, Economics, Computer Science, Mathematics, a related quantitative field, or equivalent relevant technical training.
Strong product and business judgment, with experience translating ambiguous product questions into hypotheses, analyses, experiments, and recommendations.
Deep knowledge of experimentation, causal inference, and statistical methods, including approaches appropriate for smaller or noisier datasets such as Bayesian methods.
Strong statistical judgment: you understand what the data can support, what it can't, and when additional product or business judgment is required.
Advanced SQL skills and working proficiency in Python. You don't need to be a software engineer, but you should be comfortable using code to investigate data, perform statistical analysis, and evaluate or debug AI-assisted work.
Experience working closely with Product and Engineering teams and influencing decisions rather than simply delivering analysis.
The ability to disagree constructively: you can push back when the evidence warrants it, communicate uncertainty clearly, and maintain strong working relationships with cross-functional partners.
A track record of independently identifying opportunities and driving analytical work from problem framing through recommendation and impact.

Experience with e-commerce, merchant products, inventory systems, seller tools, or two-sided marketplaces is a plus, but not required.

Bonus signals we look for

You've questioned an existing approach and built something better rather than copying what was done before.

Description

At Amazon Selection and Catalog Systems (ASCS), our mission is to power the online buying experience for customers worldwide so they can find, discover, and buy any product they want. We innovate on behalf of our customers to ensure uniqueness and consistency of product identity and to infer relationships between products in Amazon Catalog to drive the selection gateway for the search and browse experiences on the website. We're solving a fundamental AI challenge: establishing product identity and relationships at unprecedented scale. Using Generative AI, Visual Language Models (VLMs), and multimodal reasoning, we determine what makes each product unique and how products relate to one another across Amazon's catalog. The scale is staggering: billions of products, petabytes of multimodal data, millions of sellers, dozens of languages, and infinite product diversity—from electronics to groceries to digital content.

GenAI and VLMs hold transformative promise for catalog understanding, but we operate where traditional methods fail: ambiguous problem spaces, incomplete and noisy data, inherent uncertainty, reasoning across both images and textual data, and explaining decisions at scale. Company Description

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

The Forward Deployed Engineer, Voice AI Agent Engineering designs, builds, ships, and operates voice AI agents whose core behavior is model-driven rather than explicitly authored — conversational and agentic experiences that interpret caller intent over a live audio channel, reason over context, invoke tools, and act on the caller's behalf. The engineer works across the full lifecycle: shaping ambiguous call flows and telephony requirements into precise specifications, authoring the instructions and prompts that govern voice agent behavior, proving through automated evaluation that the result behaves correctly on real calls. This is not a machine learning or AI research role — the engineer does not train foundation or speech models — but it is distinct from traditional software engineering, where systems follow deterministic call-flow logic rather than selecting execution paths at runtime.

Two things follow, and voice makes both harder. First, the agent's most important logic often lives in natural language — instructions, prompts, tool descriptions, and guardrails — which must be engineered, versioned, and reviewed with the same discipline as code, while also holding up under what a spoken channel adds: turn-taking, barge-in, and disambiguating what speech recognition got wrong. Second, because behavior is probabilistic and happens live on a call, correctness is established by measuring behavior at scale — including latency, containment, and transcription accuracy — rather than by asserting fixed outputs, making automated evaluation a first-class engineering activity rather than a quality-assurance afterthought. The engineer owns the correctness of what ships to a live caller, whether a human or an agent produced it.

What You Get To Do In This Role

Build voice AI agents. Design and ship agentic voice applications — intent interpretation, multi-step reasoning, tool invocation, and action on the caller's behalf — together with the CTI, CCaaS, and telephony integrations that make them usable in production.
Design AI-driven autonomous voice workflows. Decompose call flows and business processes into the steps and decision points a voice agent can execute — determining where autonomy is appropriate, where a live-agent handoff is required, and how misrecognition, retries, and escalation are handled.
Engineer for what voice demands. Build experiences that hold context across turns, manage barge-in and interruption, recover gracefully from speech-recognition error, disambiguate caller intent, and confirm before consequential actions — all within the latency budget a live call imposes.
Author and maintain voice agent instructions. Write, structure, and version the system instructions, role definitions, tool descriptions, guardrails, and escalation rules that govern voice agent behavior — as engineering artifacts under review and regression coverage, not configuration text.
Engineer prompts for reliability rather than demo quality. Iterate prompts against measured call outcomes: task decomposition, golden call transcripts, structured output schemas, grounding and citation, graceful hand-back to a human agent, and the token and latency cost that directly shapes caller experience.
Build automated evaluation and test non-deterministic voice behavior. Design and operate the evaluation that makes change safe on a live channel — golden call datasets, multi-turn conversation suites, model-as-judge scoring calibrated to human QA review, CI gates, and drift detection — plus adversarial, jailbreak, grounding, and tool-selection testing specific to voice.
Specify precisely and direct AI coding agents. Convert customer call-flow and telephony requirements into testable specifications with explicit scope, constraints, and acceptance criteria; decompose work into agent-sized tasks; and review agent output for correctness and maintainability. You own the result regardless of what produced it.
Deliver as a forward deployed engineer, embedded in the voice stack. Work directly inside a customer's telephony, CTI, and CCaaS environment — building against their call data, integrations, and channels, tuning instructions and evaluation sets against live traffic, and returning with evidence that improves the product.
Own quality, safety, and reliability on live calls. Monitor call containment, hallucination, unsafe actions, and transcription accuracy; defend against prompt injection and data leakage on live calls; and feed production call failures back into specifications and evaluation sets.
Collaborate across product, design, and engineering. Partner with product managers, designers and platform teams to define success criteria, align on tradeoffs, and communicate capability and risk clearly

Qualifications

To Be Successful in This Role:

A demonstrated track record of building, shipping, and operating production voice applications, including hands-on delivery of AI-native voice agent features that real callers depend on rather than demos. Direct experience authoring agentic instructions and prompts for voice, designing AI-driven autonomous call workflows, and building the evaluation and testing that verifies them against live call traffic, is required. Willingness to work directly with customers in a forward deployed capacity, embedded in their voice and contact center environment, is required. At least 10 years of experience in software engineering with at least 2 years of experience in deploying contemporary AI solutions at customers.

Education:Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. Advanced degrees or certifications are a plus but are not a substitute for a demonstrated record of shipping reliable, production voice AI agents.

Key Competencies, Skills, And Experience

Software engineering fundamentals. Strong command of data structures, algorithms, system design, APIs, data modeling, and testing.
AI native voice application development. Hands-on experience building applications where model-driven behavior is central — agent orchestration at the application layer, tool and function calling, context assembly, grounding against enterprise data, and handling the latency, cost, and failure modes unique to a live audio channel.
AI-driven autonomous workflow design. Demonstrated experience designing workflows in which voice agents carry out multi-step call processes with limited supervision: call-flow decomposition, decision points and autonomy boundaries, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, exception and retry handling, and observability over what the agent did and why.
Voice and telephony platform expertise. Practical experience with telephony integration, speech recognition and synthesis, and streaming audio — including the barge-in, turn-taking, and confirmation patterns a live call requires.
Agentic instruction authoring. Demonstrated skill writing and maintaining the natural-language logic that governs voice agent behavior — instructions, role definitions, tool descriptions, guardrails, and refusal and escalation rules — with versioning, review, and regression coverage applied as they would be to code.
Prompt engineering. Intent-driven prompt design tuned for voice: decomposition, golden and few-shot examples, structured output and schema enforcement, grounding and citation, and disciplined iteration against call-level evaluation results rather than impressions.
Evaluation and testing of non-deterministic voice systems. Ability to build measurable frameworks assessing call quality, agent behavior, tool-selection accuracy, and regression risk — golden call datasets, scenario suites, model-as-judge scoring with human QA calibration, continuous evaluation pipelines, and drift detection — plus adversarial, jailbreak, and grounding testing.
Specification precision and architectural judgment. Ability to define call-flow problems rigorously enough that another engineer or an AI agent implements them correctly, and to decide soundly when to solve a problem in code, in instructions, or by delegating to an agent.
Safety, security, and data handling. Working knowledge of risks specific to AI-integrated voice applications — prompt injection, sensitive-data and call-recording leakage, over-broad tool access, unsafe autonomous action — translated into concrete guardrails, least-privilege controls, and monitoring.
Forward deployed delivery and stakeholder communication. Comfort working directly with customers inside their telephony environment under incomplete information and fixed timelines, judgment about when a fast local solution is right and when to hold out for the durable one, and credibility communicating capability, limitation, and risk to non-engineers.

Desired Experience

Forward deployed or customer-embedded delivery. Prior work as a forward deployed engineer, solution engineer, or in professional services, delivering software inside a customer's environment.
Voice and contact center technology. Telephony and contact center platforms, IVR, speech recognition and synthesis, streaming audio, and real-time latency optimization.
Conversation design partnership. Experience working alongside conversation or content designers, contributing to dialogue flow, tone, and error-recovery design.
Evaluation and observability tooling. Evaluation frameworks, prompt and instruction management tooling, tracing for LLM applications, and analysis of production call transcripts at scale.
Enterprise domain depth. Customer service, contact center operations, sales, or enterprise workflow, at a depth sufficient to challenge a requirement rather than only implement it.

Hussh's mission: make information — especially private personal information — a real financial asset for the human it belongs to, with the human in control. - One data review gate exists and holds: every external analysis passes a senior's red pen.
- The evidence engine runs on a cadence the policy team can plan against: data in, verified analysis out.
- The company's data needs have one address — yours — with service levels instead of favors.

- Senior-level data science or data engineering with real scale behind you: pipelines serving millions, experiments at statistical seriousness, or ML systems in production.
- You have mentored a junior into a mid-level or senior — and can tell us the story. Mentorship is the job, not a nice-to-have.
- Statistical honesty under pressure. Advocacy environments test this; you have passed the test before.

- Experimentation-platform or campaign-analytics experience.
- Policy, civic-tech, or research-institution data work — evidence built for skeptical external readers.

$180,000–$240,000 base, a 10–20% target bonus, and a founding equity grant on a 4-year vest. A small, senior team by design — leverage, not headcount — where your craft compounds into a founder's growth and a campaign's credibility, at a company whose entire thesis is that information belongs to the human it describes.

Apply here on LinkedIn with your resume and a short note answering one question: describe a time the data told you something your side didn't want to hear — and what you did.

About Persona

Persona is the configurable identity platform built for businesses in a digital-first world. Verifying individuals and organizations is harder — but more important — than ever, with AI enabling fraudsters to launch sophisticated accounts at scale and regulations evolving rapidly.

We’ve built Persona to support practically every use case and industry — that’s why we’re able to serve a wide range of leading companies. For example, Reddit relies on Persona for age assurance and verification to comply with online safety regulations, protecting younger users while maintaining a seamless experience. Meanwhile, OpenAI relies on Persona to keep bad actors out, protecting one of the world’s most powerful AI platforms from large-scale abuse in a time when AI is reshaping the way we work and live.

We’re growing rapidly and looking for exceptional people to join us!

About The Role

Proving who someone is online has never been harder or more important. You'll research how to detect fraud and verify identities more accurately. Your work will include detecting AI-generated and manipulated images, understanding how models perform across populations, and finding patterns in how attackers behave.

You bring depth in at least one of computer vision, mathematics and statistics, or identity verification and fraud prevention. You test ideas with focused experiments and follow what the results show. You'll work with our ML and engineering teams to turn your findings into defenses for real customers, and you'll get to publish your work.

What You’ll Do At Persona

Lead research on open problems in identity verification and fraud prevention, using focused experiments to test new ideas quickly.
Develop methods to detect manipulated documents, AI-generated images and emerging fraud attacks.
Evaluate how reliably our models perform across different populations
Uncover the patterns in verification data that reveal fraud, and prove they're real signal and not noise.
Calibrate model confidence and measure fraud events with limited labeled data.
Partner with ML and engineering to turn research prototypes into production models.
Publish at top venues such as CVPR, NeurIPS and USENIX Security, and stay active in the research community.

What You’ll Bring To Persona

Deep expertise in one of the following:
Computer vision: research in image forensics, face analysis, generative models or representation learning.
Mathematics and statistics: strong foundation in areas such as probability, statistical inference, optimization, or applied mathematics, with experience applying it to empirical research.
Identity or fraud prevention: Experience researching identity verification, biometrics, fraud detection, out-of-distribution detection, adversarial behavior, or closely related security problems.

A PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Mathematics, Statistics, or a related technical field is strongly preferred. We will also consider candidates with an MS and an exceptional research record.
A demonstrated record of peer-reviewed publications in relevant conferences or journals, with substantive contributions to the research.
Independently lead research, design rigorous experiments, and use results including negative or unexpected findings to guide next steps.
Clear communication, including the ability to explain experimental design, findings, and limitations to technical and non-technical audiences.

Nice to haves

Research on deepfakes, presentation attacks or adversarial robustness.
Experience with noisy, imbalanced real-world data.
Experience shipping ML research to production.

Benefits And Perks

For full-time US-based employees (excluding internship and contractor opportunities), Persona offers a wide range of benefits, including medical, dental, and vision, 3% 401(k) contribution, unlimited PTO, quarterly mental health days, family planning benefits, professional development stipend, wellness benefits, among others.

For full-time UK employees, Persona offers a wide range of benefits, including private medical insurance, dental insurance, a 6% employer pension contribution, unlimited PTO, a monthly wellness stipend, professional development stipend, co-working stipend, and more.

We're one of the fastest growing marketplaces and were recently named the #1 Best Startup Employer in America by Forbes. Check out the latest Whatnot updates on our news and engineering blogs and join us as we enable anyone to turn their passion into a business and bring people together through commerce.

💻 Role

The Seller Merchant team helps sellers bring inventory onto Whatnot, organize it effectively, and make it easier to sell. That includes products, listings, variants, catalog, taxonomy, inventory creation, seller workflows, and integrations such as Shopify.

Our sellers range from someone going live for the first time on their phone to sophisticated merchants managing large inventories across multiple systems. They also operate across very different categories, countries, and selling formats. The right product experience for one seller may be completely wrong for another.

As a Data Scientist on Seller Merchant, you'll use data to help us understand those differences and build better products for sellers. Your work will ultimately help sellers become more productive, grow their businesses, and bring more high-quality supply to the marketplace.

You'll

Identify and prioritize the highest-impact opportunities to improve seller success. Use product analysis, opportunity sizing, and strategic thinking to understand where changes to seller workflows can have the largest impact on activation, inventory creation, selling efficiency, and GMV.
Design and evaluate experiments across the seller experience. Partner with Product, Engineering, and Design to turn ambiguous questions into testable hypotheses, define success metrics and guardrails, design rigorous experiments, and translate results into product decisions.
Develop the analytical frameworks that shape product strategy. Go beyond answering incoming questions by proactively identifying opportunities, defining new ways to measure seller success, and helping the team decide what to build next.
Understand how different sellers need different products. Analyze differences across seller size, maturity, category, country, inventory type, and selling format, and help determine when a single experience works versus when we should build for distinct seller segments.
Help us make good decisions even when the data isn't perfect. Supply-side problems often involve smaller samples, heterogeneous populations, or decisions where data provides important evidence without giving a black-and-white answer. You'll apply analytics, causal inference, and other statistical approaches where appropriate, while partnering closely with product leaders to combine evidence with sound judgment.

You'll be deeply embedded with the product team, but you'll also have meaningful independence to develop your own hypotheses, challenge existing thinking, and use data to influence where the team invests.

We offer flexibility to work from home or from one of our global office hubs, and we value in-person time for planning, problem-solving, and connection. Team members in this role must live within commuting distance of our New York, San Francisco hub.

👋 You

People who do well at Whatnot tend to be comfortable figuring things out as they go, biased toward action, and genuinely curious about what they're building. They care more about outcomes than credit and stay close to the product and the people using it.

As Our Next Data Scientist, You Should Have 5+ Years Of Experience In Product Data Science, Analytics, Or a Closely Related Field, Plus

A Bachelor's degree in Statistics, Economics, Computer Science, Mathematics, a related quantitative field, or equivalent relevant technical training.
Strong product and business judgment, with experience translating ambiguous product questions into hypotheses, analyses, experiments, and recommendations.
Deep knowledge of experimentation, causal inference, and statistical methods, including approaches appropriate for smaller or noisier datasets such as Bayesian methods.
Strong statistical judgment: you understand what the data can support, what it can't, and when additional product or business judgment is required.
Advanced SQL skills and working proficiency in Python. You don't need to be a software engineer, but you should be comfortable using code to investigate data, perform statistical analysis, and evaluate or debug AI-assisted work.
Experience working closely with Product and Engineering teams and influencing decisions rather than simply delivering analysis.
The ability to disagree constructively: you can push back when the evidence warrants it, communicate uncertainty clearly, and maintain strong working relationships with cross-functional partners.
A track record of independently identifying opportunities and driving analytical work from problem framing through recommendation and impact.

Experience with e-commerce, merchant products, inventory systems, seller tools, or two-sided marketplaces is a plus, but not required.

You've questioned an existing approach and built something better rather than copying what was done before.
You've owned outcomes end-to-end, not just tasks within a narrow scope.
You've stepped outside your job description to solve a problem because it needed to get done.
You use Whatnot as a buyer or seller and can speak to the product with real context.
You've worked on a marketplace, platform, or product where meaningfully different user groups required different product experiences or analytical approaches.
You've made consequential product recommendations in situations where the data was incomplete, ambiguous, or statistically challenging.

Compressed career growth. Short feedback loops, real ownership, and problems no one has solved before mean you learn faster. People regularly say one year here equals three elsewhere, and high performers take on more responsibility quickly.

About the Role

We are looking for a Principal AI Researcher
to join our growing AI team and help build intelligent, production-grade AI systems that solve complex problems at scale.

.

A Day in the Life

You take an idea from paper to prototype to production. If you have only ever done one of those three, this role will stretch you, and we are fine with that if the rest is strong.
You can build the model layer of a real product, not just a model. That means choosing model sizes, composing several models into a working system, and holding a product-level accuracy bar.
You write real code. Python fluently, PyTorch fluently, and enough systems sense to know why your training run is slow.
You design experiments. You state the hypothesis, run the ablation, and report the result that disagrees with you.
You measure things. You are suspicious of results that look good, and you build the eval before you build the model.
You read current research and can tell the difference between a technique that will hold up and one that will not.
You explain your work to people who are not AI engineers, including clinicians and operators who will tell you when your output is wrong.

What You Need

MS or PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, or a related quantitative field. Exceptional BS candidates with substantial research or open-source work will be considered.
Depth beyond coursework: first-author publications at NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, or similar; meaningful open-source ML contributions; a research internship at an AI lab; or models you trained and shipped that people actually used.
You have fine-tuned an open-weight model yourself, understand the difference between parameter-efficient and full fine-tuning, and can explain why you chose one.
Strong Python and PyTorch. Familiarity with the current training and serving stack (HuggingFace, FSDP or DeepSpeed, vLLM or SGLang, or equivalents).
Some exposure to multi-GPU training, even at lab scale. You should know what a sharding strategy is and why it matters.
Evidence you can finish things.
You have post-trained models that ran in production and you know what broke.

You have designed the complete model architecture behind a shipped product, spanning small, medium, and large models, and made the tier and composition decisions that determined whether it worked economically.
You have made the calls that decide whether a model program works: data mixture, objective design, when to stop a run, when to abandon an approach that a team is emotionally invested in.
Deep familiarity with large-scale distributed training failure modes and the operational discipline that keeps a long run alive.
A public or verifiable record: papers, model releases, systems, or a training program whose results speak for themselves.
You can set a two-to-four-quarter technical direction and then get a team to execute it. You will effectively define what in-house modeling means at Innovaccer.
